A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ToMMeR work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original mention-detection and full-NER experiments, layer/model/rank analyses, and human validation of 1,800 spans.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds WikiANN evaluations, runtime measurements, and bias-corrected precision estimates.

M1.justification: The frozen-backbone cosine-matching probe, span features, balanced loss, self-distillation, and decoding procedures remain unchanged. Section 5 newly documents cross-entropy and a non-entity label for the existing NER setup; this does not establish a method revision.

E1.justification: Table 1 adds actual WikiANN evaluations in English, Spanish, French, German, and Chinese alongside the retained 13 benchmarks. This substantially extends demonstrated coverage to explicit cross-language and cross-script transfer, beyond the multilingual dataset descriptions already present in v1.

E2.justification: New Appendix B evaluates a Llama-3.2-1B prompting baseline using UniversalNER's extraction prompt in a runtime comparison. The GLiNER and EMBER comparators in Table 3 and the existing architecture comparisons are unchanged.

E3.justification: New evaluations use 40,000 samples per WikiANN language and introduce a single-passage timing protocol with a 24 GB GPU, Hugging Face Transformers, and a 100-token generation cap for prompting. Existing benchmark decoding, model configurations, and training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix E adds preliminary normalization ablations reporting inferior performance with arctan and log-sigmoid. Appendix I and Figure 15 add annotation-schema examples. Existing rank, layer, architecture, and ACE prediction analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Section 4.2 and Table 2 introduce Prediction-Powered Inference bias correction and 95% uncertainty reporting for the central precision estimate. v1 reported raw judge precision and agreement statistics only. The five annotators and 1,800 human judgments are unchanged; additional annotations or repeated runs are not established.

E6.justification: New results include WikiANN threshold recall of 91.3% for German and 40.7% for Chinese, corrected precision of 90.80% on MultiNERD and 87.13% on GENIA, and single-passage timings of 3.21 seconds for prompting versus 0.077 seconds for ToMMeR. Original benchmark and full-NER scores remain unchanged; the corrected precision values are re-estimates, not model performance gains.

T1.justification: Appendix B adds an explicit complexity argument asserting O(N) span classification versus O(NM) generation, plus an approximate 2.6-fold early-layer truncation calculation. The existing mathematical definitions and model equations remain unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The central early-layer probing contribution remains. The introduction and conclusion add Latin-script transfer and a 42-fold prompting-speed claim, while the abstract qualifies precision as an estimated 90% under a human-calibrated judge protocol.

C2.justification: v2 expands the ACE explanation to include missing pronouns, attributes weaker Chinese transfer to tokenization and the English-centric backbone, and discusses judge circularity and bias correction. Appendices E and I add explanations for cosine normalization and differences between annotation schemas.

D1.justification: v2 changes the reproducibility statement from a future release to stated code/model publication. It also documents the existing NER fine-tuning sequence, cross-entropy and non-entity class, and supplies the runtime prompt, passage, hardware capacity, and generation cap. Core training configurations are retained.

R1.justification: Adds Angelopoulos et al. on PPI, Thakur et al. on judge reliability, and Sakata, Bai, and Hammal et al. on related entity-probing and NER approaches. These locally broaden positioning; the updated UniversalNER bibliography refers to the same previously cited work.

P1.justification: The introduction and conclusion are reworked, judge-evaluation prose is streamlined, and Section 2 subheadings are consolidated. The overall section sequence and most technical exposition remain intact; existing appendices are renumbered around the new efficiency and schema-comparison sections.

P2.justification: Table 1 adds a WikiANN block and gray precision/F1 values; Table 2 is transposed and expanded for bias correction and bounds. Figure 15 is new. v1 Figure 5 moves to the appendix as v2 Figure 6, while the original diagrams and plots are retained.

improvement.justification: WikiANN results expose weaker Chinese transfer, added NER details aid reproduction, and explicit bias correction makes the earlier raw judge-precision claim more transparent. These gains are limited by inconsistent uncertainty reporting: Table 2 gives an aggregate lower bound of 88.11%, while Limitations claims above 89%. The broad 42-fold speed claim also rests on one passage with different output requirements for prompting and mention detection.
